_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
A stale "tool-pills" feature flag override still renders bursts of tool calls as inline cards. The page's localStorage already holds the override ff:tool-pills = "true" (do not set it yourself). The conversation at /c/{{ID}} is a generated one whose turns each contain several consecutive tool calls: the burst shape that used to collapse into one pill row. "The cards" are the elements matching '[data-testid="tool-call-completed"], [data-testid="tool-call-running"]', in document order. Perform the steps in order.
1. Navigate to /c/{{ID}} and wait for the message input ([data-testid="message-input"]) to be visible (allow 30s).
2. The override really is in place: localStorage.getItem("ff:tool-pills") is exactly "true".
3. Wait until there are more than 1 cards (allow 30s): every tool call is an inline card (or its cheap geometry placeholder, for the ones far offscreen).
4. There are no ".tool-pill", no ".tool-pills-row" and no ".tool-detail-modal" elements (count 0 each).
5. Two tool calls from the same burst sit next to each other in the stream, each as its own full-width card rather than side by side in a row: in an eval with expect "true", each of the first two cards has getBoundingClientRect().width greater than 0.5 times the messages container's (".messages-container") clientWidth.

steps.expression: (() => { const cards = document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="tool-call-completed"], [data-testid="tool-call-running"]'); const container = document.querySelector('.messages-container'); if (!container || cards.length < 2) return 'false'; const containerWidth = container.clientWidth; const w0 = cards[0].getBoundingClientRect().width; const w1 = cards[1].getBoundingClientRect().width; return (w0 > 0.5 * containerWidth && w1 > 0.5 * containerWidth) ? 'true' : 'false'; })()
